production.note: UK-market record, so calendar years. Start: Lotus's September 2021 release says 'Production of the Lotus Emira V6 First Edition will start in the spring' (lotus-emira-v6-first-edition-release), and Evo refers to 'the car's 2022 launch'. No opened page states the exact date the first customer car was built. Still on sale: Evo's review dated 12 Aug 2026 lists the V6 as a current model ('Now available in Turbo, Turbo SE, V6 and 420 Sport guises'), and lotuscars.com lists the Emira V6 SE (lotus-us-emira-page). The car is also sold in the US: Carscoops reported the V6 First Edition at $93,900 for the US (carscoops-emira-us-price). US model years were not confirmed from an opened page.

body.note: 'an all-new mid-engine premium sports car'; fixed-roof two-seater, no open version.

configuration.note: 'Supercharged 3.5-litre 400hp V6'. Toyota 2GR-FE per Motor1 (motor1-emira-v6-specs). The four-cylinder Emira (i4 / Turbo) is a separate variant.

drivetrain.note: Mid-engined, rear-wheel drive; inferred from the description of the car ('mid-engined chassis').

transmission.note: 'six-speed manual transmission as standard, optional six-speed auto with paddleshift'. The automatic is a torque-converter gearbox.

powerHp.note: Quote: "Developing 400hp, it's mated to a six-speed manual gearbox with a visible gearchange mechanism and hydraulic power-assisted steering." Lotus states the figure in hp in its home-market release; Carscoops gives the equivalents as '400 hp (298 kW / 405 PS)' (carscoops-emira-us-price). 298 kW x 1.34102 = 400 hp; 405 PS x 0.98632 would round to 399, so Lotus's own hp figure is used as published. Evo's specification table also prints '400bhp @ 6800rpm'. The same 400 hp was announced for the US car.

weightLb.note: 1,457 kg x 2.20462 = 3,212 lb. Lotus's claimed kerb weight as printed in Evo's specification table. Quote: "V6, 3456cc, supercharged | 400bhp @ 6800rpm | 310lb ft @ 3500rpm | 1457kg (claimed)"; Evo's text: "the 1457kg kerb weight (or 1486kg, as measured on our scales)". Evo does not say whether the figure is DIN or EU, or which gearbox; the table's 310 lb ft torque is the manual car's. No Lotus page stating a kerb weight could be opened (media.lotuscars.com redirects), so this is a publication figure and confidence is medium. No US-market curb weight from Lotus or a major magazine could be opened, which is why the record uses the UK market throughout.

reviewNotes: Market: the Emira V6 is sold in the US, where the guide calls for a US-market record, but no US curb weight from Lotus or a major magazine's specification panel could be opened (Car and Driver, MotorTrend and Road & Track are blocked). To avoid mixing markets the record uses the UK home market for both power (Lotus release, 400hp) and weight (Lotus's claimed 1,457 kg as printed by Evo). A human should decide whether to keep the UK basis or re-source a US curb weight and US model years. Also: Evo does not state whether 1,457 kg is a DIN or EU figure, and the production start year rests on Lotus's forward-looking 'will start in the spring' (release of September 2021) plus Evo's '2022 launch'.
